TASK-MIG-005.notes: Reworked bounded, transient model-led elicitation (src/histgerm/research/elicitation.py) so malformed model output is recovered candidate-locally instead of discarding valid work. The whole-response candidate list is now parsed independently of the candidates it contains (_ResponseEnvelope validates only the {"candidates": [...]} envelope with extra='forbid'/strict), and each candidate is validated on its own via _CandidateOutput: one malformed sibling (extra field, URL/control-char name, wrong type, non-object entry) becomes a scoped ElicitationQuarantine (scope='candidate', deterministic 1-based position, stable reason, best-effort raw name) while every valid sibling is retained. Invalid response formatting (non-JSON, wrong envelope shape, a non-list candidates value, or oversize output) is retried exactly once with a schema-feedback prompt that echoes the exact rejection reason and re-states the name-only contract; a recovered retry yields leads and after retry exhaustion the response becomes a scope='response' quarantine that contributes no leads (no success-shaped fallback). Safe count-limit excess is truncated with an explicit warning: max_candidates_per_response drops surplus entries and max_aliases_per_candidate trims surplus aliases while keeping the lead. Deterministic ElicitationMetrics (retries_attempted/recovered, responses_blocked, candidates_quarantined, candidates_truncated, aliases_truncated) and warnings/quarantines are exposed on ElicitationResult as additive, default-valued fields (existing leads/prompts/requires_external_search unchanged), ElicitationPrompt.kind widens to include 'retry', and ElicitationOutputError stays exported and is still raised loudly when the injected model returns a non-string (a dependency-contract violation, never a recoverable model formatting error). DiscoveryCoverage gains elicitation_retries/recovered_retries/blocked_responses/quarantined_candidates counters surfaced through snapshot() and DiscoveryRunResult.as_json, wired from ElicitationResult.metrics in run_discovery. Provider-gap and trusted-evidence semantics are untouched (elicitation still produces only untrusted name-only leads requiring external search). New/updated tests cover malformed arrays, malformed objects/siblings, URL/wrong-type names, invalid-JSON-then-valid retry recovery, repeated-invalid scoped blocking, candidate- and alias-count truncation warnings, oversize retry recovery, non-string loud rejection, the surviving exclusion-name bound, the new metrics snapshot keys, and an end-to-end run_discovery worker-result path that keeps a valid lead beside a quarantined sibling and surfaces the metrics. No serialized ledger/vocabulary/checkpoint format, public exception type, or CLI exit code changed; no live ledger/vocabulary/inventory YAML changed.

TASK-MIG-006.notes: Made discovery protocol failures resumable without discarding confirmed work. discovery_session.apply_exchange keeps fatal handling for a wrong run identifier, an unknown or replayed request, a mismatched capability type, and duplicate or unrequested inspection positions, so no response can ever apply to the wrong item or run. A revision mismatch (stale or future) now raises the new StaleCheckpointError, a DiscoveryProtocolError subclass carrying run_id, expected_revision, and the current outstanding requests, so the coordinator receives actionable current-state output instead of a discarded run. An inspection response that classifies only some requested positions is accepted: answered positions are recorded by item digest and the unanswered positions re-defer, so the memo re-offers exactly the missing items as a strictly smaller batch on the next advance; an entirely unanswered request stays a fatal missing response. The memo splits deferred inspection pages into successive bounded batches no larger than INSPECTION_BATCH_LIMIT (default 20) via itertools.batched, which also removes the latent >MAX_INSPECTION_ITEMS request-construction crash. discovery_runtime._provider_fetch now turns lower-level OSError/TimeoutError transport failures (alongside the existing MetadataFetchError path) into structured, body-less provider-gap ProviderResponses so one channel's transport gap never aborts the others, while a wrong argument type still raises TypeError. New tests/research/test_discovery_recovery.py drives all GATE-RECOVERY requirements end to end through the resumable state machine (evidence-grounded dispositions, canonical query intents, malformed-sibling retention, single-retry formatting recovery, missing-position smaller-batch retry, bounded batch splitting, provider-gap continuation, stale/future actionable output, wrong-run fatality, and resume without repeating confirmed retrieval); test_discovery_runtime.py adds the OSError provider-gap adapter case. TASK-MIG-007.notes: Introduced a typed, versioned, append-only run journal in two new modules under src/histgerm/research/. run_journal.py owns the fixed event envelope (schema_version, run_id, sequence, recorded_at, kind, payload) and thirteen discriminated payload kinds (run_started, query_planned, query_executed, provider_gap, lead_found, model_response_invalid, retry_scheduled, candidate_blocked, candidate_researched, ledger_revision_observed, ledger_mutation_proposed, checkpoint, run_completed) as strict extra='forbid' models under one kind-discriminated union, plus canonical byte-stable line encoding, the SHA-256 journal content hash reproduced identically for writing and hashing, a deterministic order-sensitive replay reduction (replay_journal -> JournalReplay), and the generated validation JSON Schema whose canonical serialization is stored as tests/research/fixtures/journal_event_schema.txt and hashed in artifacts.journal. journal_store.py provides durable, atomic, interruption-safe append reusing the TASK-MIG-004 write_durable_temporary + replace_atomically primitives under a journal-locks-v1 bounded OS advisory lock: append is idempotent on an identical (run_id, sequence) and raises JournalConflictError on a conflicting duplicate, a wrong run identifier, a sequence gap, or an expected_last_sequence mismatch (optimistic concurrency); read_journal recovers a single torn trailing line (an interrupted append) while raising JournalCorruptionError on mid-file corruption, a non-UTF-8 body, a sequence gap, a wrong run identifier, a missing/duplicate run_started, or a stale checkpoint hash/last_sequence; compact_journal appends a verifiable checkpoint retaining the prior content hash and last sequence, idempotent on an already-checkpointed tail; and validate_journal_path requires a *.journal.jsonl operational path outside the histgerm package so the artifact stays out of trusted inventory data and every distribution. __main__.py adds the JSON-only journal-validate/journal-status/journal-append/journal-compact subcommands, each emitting exactly one JSON object, with new nonzero exit codes journal_conflict=3, invalid_journal_path=2, invalid_journal=2, and filesystem_error=4, while every existing CLI command, exit code, and serialized ledger/vocabulary/checkpoint format is unchanged. tests/research/test_run_journal.py covers interrupted-append validity via a monkeypatched os.replace, schema/version/event typing, deterministic and order-sensitive replay, torn-tail recovery versus fatal mid-file/gap/wrong-run/non-UTF-8/first-event corruption, idempotent versus conflicting append, optimistic-concurrency conflicts, verifiable and tamper-detecting checkpoints, cross-process concurrent append without lost updates, path safety, CLI single-JSON output and exit codes, and the recorded schema-artifact hash. No live ledger/vocabulary/inventory YAML changed (ledger revision 95, vocabulary revision 0 unchanged).

persistence.description: Shared durable, atomic, single-writer persistence primitives extracted for TASK-MIG-004 and reused by the ledger, vocabulary store, and checkpoint writer.
primitives: write_durable_temporary: same-directory mkstemp, write, flush, os.fsync, optional chmod; cleans up and re-raises the original error on failure.
replace_atomically: os.replace with prior-content-preserving cleanup that re-raises the original error so the caller reports its own atomic-replace failure.
remove_temporary: unlink tolerating only prior absence.
stable_lock_path: deterministic per-target lock path outside the target directory, distinct per target and namespace.
bounded_file_lock: bounded OS-backed exclusive advisory lock on a never-evicted lock file; the kernel releases it on owner exit so a crash leaves no stale lock and no unsafe deletion is required.

consumers.ledger: namespace 'ledger-locks-v1'; preserves LedgerWriteError/LedgerRevisionError/LedgerPolicyError and byte-stable canonical YAML.
consumers.vocabulary: namespace 'vocabulary-locks-v1'; replaces the O_CREAT|O_EXCL next-to-file lock, so no '.<name>.lock' is created and a crashed owner is handled without deletion.
consumers.checkpoint: adds flush + os.fsync while keeping 0o600 permissions, the '.histgerm-' temp prefix, the size bound, and original-exception re-raise on OS failure.

persistence.serialization_diff: none: no ledger, vocabulary, or checkpoint serialized format, public exception type, or CLI exit code changed, so no artifact hash is required for this task.

elicitation_recovery.description: Candidate-local model-output recovery for TASK-MIG-005: malformed sibling output never discards valid candidate leads, and unrecoverable output becomes an explicit, deterministic quarantine instead of an exception or a success-shaped fallback.
primitives: _ResponseEnvelope: validates only the {"candidates": [...]} envelope (extra='forbid', strict) so individual candidates are parsed independently; a non-JSON body, wrong envelope shape, non-list candidates value, or oversize output is returned as a soft _EnvelopeError, never a raise.

_elicit_response: retries invalid response formatting exactly once with a schema-feedback prompt (ElicitationPrompt kind='retry') that echoes the exact rejection reason; a recovered retry yields leads, and after retry exhaustion the response becomes a scope='response' ElicitationQuarantine contributing no leads.

_add_output_leads: validates each candidate via _CandidateOutput; a malformed sibling becomes a scope='candidate' ElicitationQuarantine (deterministic 1-based position, stable reason, best-effort raw name) while valid siblings are retained; max_candidates_per_response and max_aliases_per_candidate excess is truncated with an explicit warning.
_call_model: raises the still-exported ElicitationOutputError only when the injected model returns a non-string (a dependency-contract violation, never a recoverable model formatting error).

result_additions.ElicitationResult: additive default-valued fields quarantines: tuple[ElicitationQuarantine, ...] = (), warnings: tuple[str, ...] = (), metrics: ElicitationMetrics = ElicitationMetrics(); existing leads/prompts/requires_external_search are unchanged and still keyword-constructed.
result_additions.ElicitationMetrics: retries_attempted, retries_recovered, responses_blocked, candidates_quarantined, candidates_truncated, aliases_truncated.

elicitation_recovery.metrics_integration: DiscoveryCoverage gains elicitation_retries/elicitation_recovered_retries/elicitation_blocked_responses/elicitation_quarantined_candidates, surfaced through snapshot() and DiscoveryRunResult.as_json and wired from ElicitationResult.metrics in run_discovery.
elicitation_recovery.invariants_preserved: Elicitation still yields only untrusted, name-only leads requiring external search; provider-gap and trusted-evidence semantics are untouched; no partially validated trusted record is ever accepted; no serialized format, public exception type, or CLI exit code changed.
elicitation_recovery.serialization_diff: none: elicitation output is transient and unpersisted, so no artifact hash is required for this task.

protocol_recovery.description: Resumable protocol failures for TASK-MIG-006: every recoverable failure preserves confirmed positions and retrievals and resumes without repeating confirmed work, while any recovery that could apply a response to the wrong item or run stays fatal.
primitives: StaleCheckpointError(DiscoveryProtocolError): raised by apply_exchange on any revision mismatch (stale or future); carries run_id, expected_revision, and the current outstanding requests so the coordinator receives actionable current-state output instead of a discarded run. No response is applied, so no confirmed item or run is mutated by a mismatched exchange.

apply_exchange missing-position recovery: an inspection response that classifies only some requested positions records the answered positions by item digest and leaves the rest unconfirmed; the memo re-offers exactly the missing items as a strictly smaller batch on the next advance. Duplicate positions, unrequested positions, an unknown or replayed request, a mismatched capability type, and a wrong run identifier stay fatal, and an entirely unanswered pending request stays a fatal missing response.

INSPECTION_BATCH_LIMIT (default 20) + itertools.batched: the memo splits large deferred inspection pages and smaller retry sets into successive bounded batches, giving smaller-batch retries and removing the latent >MAX_INSPECTION_ITEMS request-construction crash.

discovery_runtime._provider_fetch provider gaps: lower-level OSError/TimeoutError transport failures (alongside the existing MetadataFetchError path) become structured, body-less provider-gap ProviderResponses so one channel's transport gap never aborts the others; a wrong argument type still raises TypeError.
protocol_recovery.invariants_preserved: The checkpoint and exchange schema_version stays 1 with no field removed; DiscoveryProtocolError, apply_exchange, advance, new_checkpoint, and the request/response models keep their public shapes; the durable checkpoint format and CLI exit codes are unchanged; no live ledger/vocabulary/inventory YAML changed.
protocol_recovery.serialization_diff: none: no serialized checkpoint or exchange format changed and no new persisted structure was added (StaleCheckpointError attributes are transient), so no artifact hash is required for this task.

journal.description: Typed, versioned, append-only run journal for TASK-MIG-007: a fixed event envelope (schema_version, run_id, sequence, recorded_at, kind, payload) with thirteen discriminated payload kinds, a deterministic replay reduction, canonical byte-stable line encoding + content hash, durable atomic interruption-safe append, idempotent (run_id, sequence) append with optimistic-concurrency conflict handling, compact verifiable checkpoints, and JSON-only CLI subcommands.
primitives: run_journal.RunJournalEvent: discriminated union on kind over thirteen strict (extra='forbid') event models sharing the _EventBase envelope; EVENT_ADAPTER is the TypeAdapter used to validate one event object.

run_journal.encode_event/encode_events/journal_content_hash: canonical sort_keys JSON line encoding, newline-terminated bytes, and the SHA-256 content hash reproduced identically for writing and hashing.

run_journal.replay_journal: deterministic, order-sensitive reduction of an ordered event sequence into JournalReplay run state (counts, parameters, leads, provider gaps, blocked/researched candidates, last ledger revision, last checkpoint, completion).

run_journal.event_schema/canonical_schema_json/schema_digest: the generated validation JSON Schema, its canonical serialization stored as tests/research/fixtures/journal_event_schema.txt, and its SHA-256 digest.

journal_store.append_event: durable, atomic, interruption-safe append via the TASK-MIG-004 write_durable_temporary + replace_atomically primitives under a journal-locks-v1 bounded OS lock; idempotent on an identical (run_id, sequence) and raising JournalConflictError on a conflicting duplicate, wrong run identifier, sequence gap, or expected_last_sequence mismatch.

journal_store.read_journal: recovers a single torn trailing line (an interrupted append) while raising JournalCorruptionError on mid-file corruption, a non-UTF-8 body, a sequence gap, a wrong run identifier, a missing/duplicate run_started, or a stale checkpoint hash/last_sequence.
journal_store.compact_journal: appends a verifiable checkpoint event retaining the prior content hash and last sequence, idempotent when the journal already ends with a checkpoint.
journal_store.validate_journal_path: requires a *.journal.jsonl operational path outside the histgerm package so the artifact stays out of trusted inventory data and every distribution.

cli_subcommands.journal-validate: read + integrity-check one journal; emit schema_version, run_id, events, last_sequence, content_hash, truncated_tail (exit 0).
cli_subcommands.journal-status: emit the deterministic replay status of one journal (exit 0).
cli_subcommands.journal-append: append one JSON event from --input, optional --expected-last-sequence; emit the append outcome with idempotent flag (exit 0).
cli_subcommands.journal-compact: append a compact checkpoint; emit the outcome (exit 0).

journal.serialization_diff: additive: a new operational append-only journal format is introduced (run-journal artifacts stay excluded from every distribution by the TASK-MIG-001 globs); no existing ledger, vocabulary, or checkpoint serialized format, public exception type, or existing CLI exit code changed; no live ledger/vocabulary/inventory YAML changed.

journal_parity.description: Deterministic journal dual-write and parity for TASK-MIG-008: a pure projection of the authoritative DiscoveryRunResult into an append-only run-journal event stream, plus two symmetric reductions that make old-path and journal-replayed synthetic results equal by construction. The old exchange remains the execution authority; no live result, serialized format, or public behavior changed.
primitives: journal_adapters.discovery_run_events(config, result, *, run_id, recorded_at=None): maps one DiscoveryRunResult to an ordered, gap-free event stream (run_started at sequence 0; elicitation retries as retry_scheduled and quarantines as model_response_invalid; one query_planned plus a query_executed or provider_gap per assessment; one lead_found per retained lead; a terminal run_completed). A gap is any assessment whose Assessment is access_gap or transport_error. The mapping reads only the confirmed result, so it repeats no retrieval.

journal_adapters.synthetic_from_result / synthetic_from_events -> SyntheticDiscoveryResult: two independent reductions into the same projection (run identity, immutable scope and parameters_digest, planned and executed queries, provider gaps, retained leads with channel context, invalid model responses, retry count, terminal status). Fields the journal does not carry (vocabulary internals, pagination, completion-gap prose) are intentionally excluded so parity never depends on unrecorded information. Equality is a hard test assertion, never a runtime fallback.

journal_adapters.append_discovery_journal(path, events, *, checkpoint=False): durably appends the stream through the TASK-MIG-007 store, inheriting atomic interruption-safe append, optimistic-concurrency sequencing, and idempotent restart-resume; an optional trailing compaction checkpoint is appended and is ignored by the projection.

discovery_orchestration.DiscoveryRunResult.leads_with_context(): additive pure method projecting each retained lead as (name, url, channel, position) by the exact case-folded-URL first-seen dedup the run already uses, reproducing DiscoveryRunResult.leads while adding the originating channel.

discovery_session.completed_journal_events(checkpoint, completed, *, recorded_at=None): additive helper that builds the stream under the confirmed checkpoint.run_id and configuration for a completed resumable run.
journal_parity.parity_identity: synthetic_from_result(config, result, run_id=R) == synthetic_from_events(discovery_run_events(config, result, run_id=R)), and both equal synthetic_from_events(read_journal(path).events) after a durable round trip.
journal_parity.invariants_preserved: run_discovery, advance, apply_exchange, new_checkpoint, DiscoveryRunResult.as_json, DiscoveryProtocolError, the request/response and checkpoint models, the run-journal event schema (schema_version 1) and store, and every CLI command and exit code keep their public shapes; no serialized ledger/vocabulary/checkpoint/journal format changed and no live ledger/vocabulary/inventory YAML changed.
journal_parity.serialization_diff: none: the adapter is a transient projection over the existing TASK-MIG-007 journal format and adds no new persisted structure (SyntheticDiscoveryResult is in-memory), so no new artifact hash is required for this task.
